settings.privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.intro: This is a plain-language explanation of what happens to the information you share when you report damage through this app. By agreeing to continue, you confirm you have read and understood it.
privacy.who.title: Who runs this app
privacy.who.body: This crisis-mapping platform is operated as part of a UNDP partner program to help response teams understand where damage has occurred and direct help to where it is needed.
privacy.noAccount.title: You do not need an account
privacy.noAccount.body: You do not give us your name, email address, or phone number, and you do not log in. The app creates a random identifier on your device so you can find and delete your own reports later. It is not linked to your identity, and you can reset it any time in Settings.
privacy.collect.title: What we collect when you submit a report
privacy.collect.body:
When you choose to send a report, it includes:
• A photo you take or select. Photos can contain hidden technical information such as the location and time they were taken; we store this together with the photo.
• The location of the damage you are reporting.
• What you type: your description and any notes on how to find the place.
• Basic details about the damage, such as how severe it is and the type of structure affected.
• A random identifier created on your device.

We do not ask for, and you should not include, information that identifies you or another person unless you choose to and understand it will be visible to response coordinators.
privacy.why.title: Why we collect it
privacy.why.body: To help response coordinators see where damage has occurred, group related reports, and direct assistance. We use the information only for crisis response and coordination, not for advertising and not for any unrelated purpose.
privacy.whoSees.title: Who can see your report
privacy.whoSees.body: Response coordinators working on the crisis can see the full details of your report, including the submitted photo, location, and description. What the public map shows depends on the crisis: some show only combined totals for an area, while others may show individual reports or affected buildings. In every case the public map never shows who sent a report: no name or contact is attached, only an anonymous identifier that is never displayed publicly. You can see your own reports on the device you submitted them from.
privacy.risk.title: A note about risk
privacy.risk.body: If being identified as the person who reported damage could put you or someone else at risk, please think carefully about what you photograph and write. The public map never shows who sent a report, but a photo or description can still contain details that identify a place or a person to someone who already knows the area.
privacy.rights.title: Your choices and rights
privacy.rights.body:
• You can delete everything. In Settings, “Delete my data” permanently removes every report and photo you have submitted from this device. This cannot be undone.
• You can reset your identifier in Settings, so future reports are not linked to your past ones.
• You can stop at any time. Using the app is voluntary.
privacy.security.title: Keeping information safe
privacy.security.body: Information is sent over an encrypted connection and stored on secured infrastructure. Access to full report details is limited to authenticated response coordinators. No system is perfectly secure, and we do not promise that it is, but we limit what we collect, limit who can see it, and give you a way to delete it.
privacy.retention.title: How long we keep it
privacy.retention.body: The most reliable way to remove your information is to delete it yourself: “Delete my data” in Settings erases your reports and photos immediately, at any time. Otherwise we keep reports only for as long as they are useful to the response for the related crisis.
privacy.changes.title: Changes to this notice
privacy.changes.body: If we change this notice in a way that affects you, the app will ask you to read and agree again before you continue reporting.
privacy.questions.title: Questions
privacy.questions.body: If you have questions about how your information is handled, contact the response team through the channel they have shared with your community.
